chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying: 'For every salat are two timings, and the beginning of the time is the best of it; and it is not for anyone to make the last of the two times as his time, except in the case of an excuse without an illness.'

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: Most meritorious/superior — the early prayer time carries greater spiritual reward
key_terms.عُذْر: Excuse/dispensation — a legitimate reason that permits deferring prayer to its later time
key_terms.عِلَّة: Illness/ailment — a specific physical condition that alone does not constitute sufficient cause to prefer the late prayer time
key_terms.وَقْتَانِ: Two timings/time windows — referring to the early (preferred) and late (permissible) periods within which each obligatory prayer may be performed

ai.seo_question: What are the two prayer times in Islam and which is better according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that every obligatory prayer has two valid time windows — an earlier preferred period and a later permissible period. Performing the prayer at the beginning of its time is the most meritorious act. The Imam clarifies that delaying prayer to the later time is only permissible when there is a legitimate excuse (such as travel, forgetfulness, or pressing need), but not merely due to illness — illness being considered a lesser justification than what was traditionally understood.
